items.statement: Patients dosed with the computer-assisted tool spend more time in the therapeutic range than patients dosed with the paper nomogram, after accounting for case mix.
items.rationale: The question the director asked; feasibility is uncertain because it depends on record completeness and on a fair comparison across sites.
items.risks: Residual confounding by site; incalculable time in range for home-testing patients.

items.statement: INR and dose records are complete enough to calculate time in range for at least 80 percent of patients at each clinic.
items.rationale: A precondition for any records comparison; answerable in four weeks with approved access.
items.risks: Completeness may differ by site, which would itself bias a comparison.

items.statement: Any apparent advantage of the tool is explained by the younger, less complex patients at the satellites.
items.rationale: The alternative explanation that must be ruled out before standardising.
items.risks: Cannot be separated from h1 without allocation or rich case-mix data.

summary: h2 selected because its answer decides which design can test h1 and h3.
